To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a highly conserved Pro residue in CL7 of MRP1 (Pro1150), MRP2 (Pro1158), and MRP3 (Pro1147) is required for the transport of a variety of substrates, including LTC4, E217β, MTX, and the nucleotide analogue 8N3ADPN.
the highly conserved proline residue at position 1158 of MRP2 is important for the function of the protein and that it may play a role in the transport mechanism of MRP2.
MRP1, -2, and -3 have a conserved role for Pro1150, -1158, and -1147 in ATP hydrolysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of ATP-dependent transport in the multidrug resistance-associated protein (MRP) family of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters.
the identification of the molecular basis of drug resistance in human cancer.
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of a novel group of drug resistance genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MRP1, -2, and -3 share a conserved function in ATP binding but differ in their ability to interact with substrates.
the function of MRP1-CL7 is not fully conserved in MRP2 and in MRP3.
the MRP1 Pro1150 residue, which is located in the cytoplasmic region of CL7, is involved in the nucleotide binding and/or hydrolysis of MRP1 and the analogous residues in MRP2 and 3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MRP1, 2, and 3 are all affected by mutations at Pro1150, Pro1158, and Pro1147, respectively, in CL7 and that this is due to the fact that these prolines are all involved in ATP hydrolysis.
Pro1150 in MRP1 is critical for the transport of LTC4 and the uncoupling of nucleotide hydrolysis from substrate transport.

the CL7 Pro1150 residue of MRP1 and the corresponding Pro residues in CL7 of MRP2 and 3 are partially conserved in their functional importance for ATPase activity and transport activity of MRP1 substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pro1150 residue in MRP1 is not absolutely conserved in the function of other members of the MRP family.
a single amino acid substitution can have different effects on the transport of different organic anions.
the Pro residue in CL7 is not a universal determinant for MRP function.
